resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Returning from Functions[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

Certain functions, such as [b]int [/b]or [b]str[/b], return a value instead of outputting it. 

The returned value can be used later in the code, for example, by getting assigned to a variable. 

To do this for your defined functions, you can use the [b]return[/b] statement. Like this:
[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header][code format="py" codeId="3945"]def max(x, y):
    if x >=y:
        [b]return [/b]x
    else:
        [b]return [/b]y
        
print(max(4, 7))
z = max(8, 5)
print(z)[/code]
[note]The [b]return [/b]statement cannot be used outside of a function definition.[/note]

resolved.title: 返回return
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Returning from Functions[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

Once you return a value from a function, it immediately stops being executed. 

Any code placed after the [b]return [/b]statement won’t be executed.
[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header][code format="py" codeId="3946"]def add_numbers(x, y):
  total = x + y
  [b]return [/b]total
  print("This won't be printed")

print(add_numbers(4, 5))[/code]
[note][b]Run the code[/b] and see how it works![/note]

content.text:
一旦函数中返回一个值，它就立即停止执行。

任何放在 **return** 语句之后的代码都不会被执行。

如下：
content.text_html:
Once you return a value from a function, it immediately stops being executed.

Any code placed after the **return **statement won’t be executed. For example:

一旦你从一个函数中返回一个值，它就立即停止执行。

任何放在返回语句之后的代码都不会被执行。 例如：

content.content:
def add_numbers(x, y):
    total = x + y
    return total
    print("这一句不会被打印")

print(add_numbers(4, 5))
